title: quest task list --ready throws dependency_target_not_found for a dependency on a completed/archived task
description:
Reported inbound by opum-doc against Quest CLI 0.5.0: --ready fails with dependency_target_not_found on their workspace while quest doctor reports healthy and all 152 records scan clean. Reproduced live in this repo right now (exit 6): quest task list --ready --json fails identically, with 9 real forward-looking edges currently on disk (e.g. QCLI-138..145 -> QCLI-134, QCLI-210 -> QCLI-207), all of which are legitimate completed dependencies, not broken references.

Root cause, confirmed by reading the source: LocalTaskRepository.readAll() (src/application/tasks/local-task-repository.ts, ~line 384-393) filters snapshot.taskRecords down to location === "tasks" only when building the returned .tasks array -- it drops completed and archived records. TasksService.ready() (src/application/tasks/tasks.ts, ~line 1243) passes that filtered .tasks array straight into evaluateReadySet, which calls validateTaskGraph (src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts, ~line 625). validateTaskGraph's resolver() builds its id/alias map purely from the array it receives, so any active task depending on a task that has since relocated to .quest/completed/ (or archive/tasks/) resolves to nothing and throws dependency_target_not_found -- indistinguishable from a genuine broken forward reference.

This is why quest doctor stays healthy while --ready fails: doctor's only graph-adjacent check (planning.ts doctor(), milestone_task_not_found) reads taskSnapshot.taskRecords ?? taskSnapshot.tasks, which DOES include completed/archived, so it never hits this path. Not a regression: the filtering line has been present since the task-lifecycle/completed-relocation feature landed (fd73ade, 2026-08-17); it has likely been silently broken since then for any workspace old enough to have both open and closed dependency edges.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest task list --ready succeeds (exit 0) in this repo today, where active tasks depend on completed ones (e.g. QCLI-138..145 -> QCLI-134)
A regression test covers an active task depending on a completed/relocated task and asserts --ready no longer throws dependency_target_not_found for it
quest doctor and --ready are reconciled to use the same full-location task set for dependency-graph resolution, or the discrepancy between them is documented as deliberate with a reason

plan: 1. Fix TasksService.listFilteredLocated: compute readyIds by passing the full taskRecords-derived task set (all locations, including archive/tasks) to evaluateReadySet for graph closure, instead of the archive-excluded `listed` array; the final `filtered` result still intersects readyIds against `listed`, so archived tasks never leak into --ready output.

2. Fix TasksService.ready() the same way for consistency (readAll().tasks -> full taskRecords-derived set), since it shares the identical defect class and public API surface even though unreachable from the CLI today.

3. Add regression tests: an active task depending on a completed task (already works, keep as a non-regression check), and a task whose parentId points at an archived task while the task itself is not archived -- assert --ready/evaluateReadySet no longer throws.
4. Verify quest task list --ready succeeds in this repo (real data, 11 previously-broken parentId edges to QCLI-97).
5. Decide and record whether to reconcile quest doctor to also catch this class (a graph-validity check), or document the discrepancy as deliberate -- per AC3.
6. bun run check (typecheck, lint, format, layer:check, test) before PR.
implementationNotes: CORRECTION to the root cause in this task's description. Verified directly with a one-line diagnostic in validateTaskGraph's resolve() (temporary, reverted, never committed): the actual unresolved reference thrown by 'quest task list --ready --json' in this repo is a parentId edge, not a dependency edge -- 11 tasks (QCLI-189, QCLI-190, QCLI-204, QCLI-205, QCLI-206, QCLI-210, QCLI-211, QCLI-212, QCLI-213, QCLI-196, QCLI-207) have parentId QCLI-97, and QCLI-97 itself lives in .quest/archive/tasks/ (status To Do, independently archived -- status and location are deliberately decoupled per QCLI-221). The CLI's actual --ready path is TasksService.listFilteredLocated (tasks.ts ~486-556), not the standalone ready() method I originally cited -- that method is dead code from the CLI's perspective (only called by two tests, never by src/cli/main.ts). listFilteredLocated already includes completed-location tasks in the array passed to evaluateReadySet (QCLI-165 fixed exactly that), so a dependency on a completed task like QCLI-134/QCLI-207 resolves fine. What it does NOT include by default is archive/tasks (correctly excluded from listing unless --include-archived) -- and validateTaskGraph, called via evaluateReadySet, requires every task's parentId AND dependencies to resolve within that same filtered array, even though parenthood isn't itself a readiness edge. Any child whose parent has been archived independently of the child breaks the whole graph validation, for every task, not just that child.\n\nThe standalone ready()/readAll().tasks path I originally described is a real but separate, narrower defect (active-location only, excludes both completed AND archived) -- unreachable from the CLI today, but sharing the same public TasksService API and its own two tests, so fixing it alongside for consistency rather than leaving a second broken twin.
finalSummary:
Fixed. Corrected root cause during investigation (see the correction note above): the actually-reproducing defect on "quest task list --ready" was a parentId edge, not a dependency edge -- QCLI-97 (11 real children) lives in .quest/archive/tasks/, and validateTaskGraph (called via evaluateReadySet from TasksService.listFilteredLocated) requires every task's parentId AND dependencies to resolve within the exact array it is given. listFilteredLocated already includes completed tasks (QCLI-165) but deliberately excludes archive/tasks by default -- correct for what --ready returns, wrong as the ONLY input to graph closure, since parenthood is not itself a readiness edge but the validator does not know that until every edge resolves.

Fix: listFilteredLocated's readyIds computation and the standalone TasksService.ready() (dead code from the CLI today, but same public API and same defect) now pass the full taskRecords-derived task set (every location, including archive/tasks) into evaluateReadySet for graph-closure purposes; the returned readyIds is still only ever intersected against the archive-excluded "listed" array, so an archived task can never leak into --ready's actual output.

Verified live in this repo: "quest task list --ready --json" now exits 0 and returns QCLI-144, QCLI-145, QCLI-159, QCLI-164, QCLI-245, QCLI-247, QCLI-250 (was exit 6, dependency_target_not_found).

AC3: documented rather than reconciled. Added a code comment on planning.ts's doctor() explaining it deliberately never calls validateTaskGraph, so it can report healthy while --ready throws on the same workspace -- reconciling them would be new doctor surface, not this bug's fix.

Regression coverage: test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts adds a full CLI-level test replicating the exact production shape (archived parent with active children, plus the equivalent dependency case) and asserting --ready no longer throws and never leaks the archived task into its output. bun run check: typecheck, lint (1 pre-existing unrelated warning in qcli122-fourth-pass.test.ts, confirmed present on dev before this branch), format, layer:check all pass; 431 tests pass, 0 fail.
